42880153.label: Background
42880153.text: This study aimed to characterize sonographic hepatic findings across pediatric, adolescent, and adult Fontan patients and to examine their cross-sectional relationships with time since Fontan completion and chronological age. As a secondary objective, we explored a composite score integrating complementary sonographic findings.

42880153.label: Materials and methods
42880153.text: In this retrospective cross-sectional analysis of a prospectively established single-center Fontan cohort, hepatic ultrasound findings from 153 patients were evaluated, including gray-scale imaging, Doppler assessment, and shear-wave elastography performed according to institutional acquisition protocols. Individual sonographic findings were analyzed as the primary imaging outcomes. Cross-sectional associations with time since Fontan completion were assessed using sex-adjusted regression models; additional models simultaneously included chronological age, time since Fontan completion, and sex to examine their closely related contributions. A secondary exploratory 5-point composite score integrating five complementary sonographic domains was evaluated descriptively.

42880153.label: Results
42880153.text: Longer time since Fontan completion was associated cross-sectionally with greater IVC diameter, liver size, shear-wave velocity, structural abnormality, and hepatic nodularity in sex-adjusted analyses. Chronological age and time since Fontan completion were nearly collinear (r = 0.970). When both variables and sex were included simultaneously, associations with IVC diameter, liver size, shear-wave velocity, and structural classification were attenuated and no longer statistically significant, whereas hepatic nodularity remained associated with time since Fontan completion (OR = 1.22/year; 95% CI 1.03-1.45; p = 0.024). Complete composite-score data were available in 101 patients; mean scores were 0.81 ± 0.88, 2.15 ± 1.26, 3.18 ± 0.80, and 4.27 ± 0.80 across < 5-, 5-<10-, 10-<20-, and ≥ 20-year post-Fontan categories, respectively. In 15 patients with serial examinations, scores were higher at the later examination in 10 and unchanged in five (p = 0.004). In a stratified subset of 40 independently reread examinations, interobserver agreement was high for liver size (ICC = 0.922) and IVC diameter (ICC = 0.947), whereas agreement for qualitative sonographic findings was lower (κ = 0.202-0.369).

42880153.label: Conclusion
42880153.text: Sonographic vascular, morphologic, structural, elastographic, and nodular abnormalities differed across patients examined at increasing intervals after Fontan completion. However, because chronological age and Fontan duration were nearly collinear, this cross-sectional study cannot determine whether these imaging gradients reflect duration of Fontan physiology, chronological maturation, or both. Hepatic nodularity showed the most robust association with time since Fontan completion in simultaneous models. The composite score provides a secondary exploratory framework for integrating complementary sonographic findings but requires prospective longitudinal and external validation. The limited interobserver agreement for qualitative findings further emphasizes the need for standardized image interpretation and supports the exploratory status of the composite score.

42891703.label: Purpose
42891703.text: Postoperative lymphoceles are recognized complications of retroperitoneal lymph node dissection (RPLND) for testicular germ cell tumours (TGCT). Previous studies have predominantly reported symptomatic or intervention-requiring lymphoceles, whereas the incidence, temporal evolution, and clinical relevance of lymphoceles on postoperative imaging remain poorly defined. We evaluated radiologically detected lymphoceles and clinically relevant lymphatic complications after post-chemotherapy RPLND (PC-RPLND) using routine serial imaging.

42891703.label: Methods
42891703.text: This retrospective single-centre cohort study included 86 consecutive patients who underwent PC-RPLND under a standardized perioperative management protocol. Postoperative imaging consisted of ultrasound at postoperative day 5-7 and 3-4 weeks, followed by computed tomography at 3 and 12 months. The primary endpoint was the incidence of any imaging-detected lymphocele during follow-up. Secondary endpoints included lymphocele prevalence at each imaging time point, clinically relevant lymphatic complications, postoperative complications, and exploratory factors associated with lymphocele formation.

42891703.label: Results
42891703.text: Of 86 included patients, 85 were evaluable for the primary endpoint. Overall, 46 patients (54.1%) had at least one imaging-detected lymphocele during follow-up. Lymphoceles were most frequently detected at discharge (36/84, 42.9%) and decreased over time to 32.8% (19/58) at 3-4 weeks, 31.5% (17/54) at 3 months, and 15.8% (9/57) at 12 months. Clinical follow-up was available for 65 patients. Clinically relevant lymphatic complications occurred in only 3 patients (4.6%), comprising two cases of lymphatic/chylous ascites and one lymphatic fistula associated with a small precaval lymphocele. Among 49 patients with paired 3- and 12-month CT, 10 of 16 lymphoceles present at 3 months had resolved by 12 months, whereas only one was newly detected (exact McNemar p = .012). Exploratory analyses identified no significant associations between imaging-detected lymphocele formation and patient characteristics, tumour-related factors, surgical approach, or extent of lymphadenectomy.

42891703.label: Conclusions
42891703.text: Lymphoceles are frequently detected by routine serial imaging after PC-RPLND but rarely translate into clinically relevant lymphatic morbidity. Radiologically detected lymphoceles should therefore be distinguished from clinically relevant lymphatic complications when interpreting surveillance imaging, counselling patients, and reporting postoperative outcomes after RPLND.

42899353.label: Background
42899353.text: Recent advances in artificial intelligence enable fully automated 3-dimensional computed tomography (CT)-based body composition quantification. We investigated whether automated CT-derived thoraco-abdominopelvic body composition measures are associated with mortality after transcatheter aortic valve replacement.

42899353.label: Methods
42899353.text: In this retrospective multicenter study, consecutive patients undergoing transcatheter aortic valve replacement with preprocedural CT imaging were included between 2014 and 2023. A deep learning-based pipeline performed automated 3-dimensional segmentation of thoraco-abdominopelvic noncontrast CT scans to quantify volumes (L/m2) and attenuations (Hounsfield units) of subcutaneous adipose tissue, visceral adipose tissue, muscular adipose tissue, and lean skeletal muscle, indexed to body surface area. Associations with mortality were evaluated using Cox models and Harrell C statistics, adjusting for demographics (age, sex, body mass index) and cardiometabolic risk factors (hypertension, diabetes, chronic renal failure).

42899353.label: Results
42899353.text: Among 915 patients (median age, 84 years [interquartile range, 77-90]; 58% men), 160 (17.5%) died over a median follow-up of 22 months (interquartile range, 14-36). Restricted cubic spline analyses demonstrated that lower subcutaneous adipose tissue volume and higher adipose tissue attenuation were associated with increased mortality, whereas higher skeletal muscle volume and attenuation were associated with improved survival. Addition of body composition measures provided incremental discriminatory value beyond demographics and cardiometabolic risk factors (Harrell C, 0.66 versus 0.71; P<0.001).

42899353.label: Conclusions
42899353.text: Automated 3-dimensional CT-derived body composition measures provide independent prognostic information and improve risk stratification for mortality after transcatheter aortic valve replacement. Low subcutaneous adipose tissue volume and higher adipose tissue attenuation identify patients at increased risk, whereas higher skeletal muscle volume and attenuation are associated with lower mortality.

42912553.text: Intussusception of bowel in adults is relatively rare and most commonly secondary to gastrointestinal malignancies. We present the case of an 80-year-old man with rectosigmoid adenocarcinoma evaluated via 18 F-FDG PET/CT. Imaging revealed rectosigmoid intussusception with a characteristic "target sign" on both PET and CT images involving the invaginated bowel, alongside synchronous FDG-avid lung metastases. Subsequent MRI confirmed the anatomical findings. This case highlights the unique utility of hybrid 18 F-FDG PET/CT in simultaneously delineating both malignant and nonmalignant metabolic and anatomical changes and providing critical whole-body staging to guide clinical management.

42963303.label: Background
42963303.text: In patients with coronary artery disease (CAD), both functional and anatomical assessment are required to guide revascularization. Computed tomography-derived fractional flow reserve (FFR-CT) has emerged as a tool to implement both anatomical and non-invasive functional assessment of coronary stenoses in a single setting, but the association with long-term outcomes is still controversial. We aimed to assess the correlation between FFR-CT with long-term outcomes in patients with CAD.

42963303.label: Methods
42963303.text: Reconstructed individual patient data were provided by the authors of a previous report published in a previous issue of the Journal. The primary outcome was study-defined major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE), while secondary outcomes included the single components of the primary outcome. One-stage and two-stage meta-analyses with mixed-effect and random-effect models were conducted, stratifying patients according to FFR-CT thresholds of 0.8. Heterogeneity sources were explored through sensitivity analyses.

42963303.label: Results
42963303.text: Fifteen studies were pooled from the reconstructed data, encompassing a total of 14,437 patients, with 6335 (43.9%) having a FFR-CT<0.8. After a median follow-up of 16.8 (7.2-35.8) months, FFR-CT<0.8 was associated with higher rates of MACE (hazard ratio: 4.93; 95% CI 4.16-5.84; p < 0.001), myocardial infarction (incidence rate ratio [IRR] 4.38; 95% CI 1.16-16.54; p = 0.029), ischemia driven revascularization (IRR 2.90; 95% CI 1.31-6.44; p = 0.009), and any revascularization (IRR 9.62; 95% CI 3.02-30.61; p < 0.001). Results were consistent across sensitivity analyses.

42963303.label: Conclusions
42963303.text: In patients with CAD, an FFR-CT <0.80 is associated with a three-to four-fold increase in MACE, being primarily driven by significant increase in myocardial infarction, ischemia-driven revascularization and any revascularization.

42975303.text: Background Microwave ablation (MWA) combined with ethanol injection (EI) is a minimally invasive technique under preliminary investigation for the treatment of nodular retrosternal goiter (RSG) and has shown promising treatment efficacy. However, a comparative analysis between ablation and surgery is warranted to draw definitive conclusions. Purpose To compare the long-term efficacy and safety of MWA combined with EI versus surgery for patients with nodular RSG. Materials and Methods This retrospective study included patients with nodular RSG treated with MWA combined with EI or surgery between October 2016 and June 2024. Propensity score matching was performed for patients in the ablation and surgery groups, followed by comparisons between the two groups with independent-sample t test, Mann-Whitney U test, χ2, or Fisher exact test. Primary outcomes were treatment success, symptom score, and complication rate. Secondary outcomes were cosmetic score, hospitalization, procedure time, estimated blood loss, incision length, and cost. Results This study included 555 patients (mean age ± SD, 51 years ± 14.4; 414 women). After propensity score matching, 224 patients in the ablation group and 224 patients in the surgery group were observed for a median of 48 months (IQR, 24-60 months). No evidence of a difference was observed in the treatment success rates between the ablation and surgery group (98.7% [221 of 224] vs 100% [224 of 224], respectively; P = .08), while both modalities effectively lowered symptom scores from baseline (both P < .001). Compared with surgery, MWA resulted in a lower complication rate (2.2% [five of 224] vs 34.8% [78 of 224], P < .001), shorter posttreatment hospitalization (P < .001), shorter procedure time (P < .001), reduced estimated blood loss (P < .001), shorter incision length (P < .001), lower cost (P < .001), and lower cosmetic score (mean, 1.1 ± 0.3 vs 1.2 ± 0.4; P = .03) at the 12-month follow-up. Conclusion MWA combined with EI was as effective as surgery for nodular RSGs, providing comparable symptom relief while demonstrating fewer complications, offering a safer alternative for eligible patients.

42993453.label: Objectives
42993453.text: Preoperative identification of FIGO 2023 stage I endometrial cancer (EC) is important for treatment planning. We aimed to develop and validate a deep-learning radiomics nomogram (DLRN) based on multiparametric MRI to distinguish stage I EC from stage II-IV disease.

42993453.label: Materials and methods
42993453.text: This study retrospectively enrolled patients from three centers. Patients from Centers 1 and 2 were randomly split into a training set (n = 616), and an internal test set (n = 158), and Center 3 served as an external test set (n = 232). The DLRN integrated deep-learning features, intratumoral and peritumoral radiomics features, and clinical characteristics. The DLRN was compared with clinical, radiomics, and deep-learning models. Discrimination was evaluated using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), with AUCs compared using DeLong's test.

42993453.label: Results
42993453.text: A total of 1006 patients (mean age, 56.5 ± 9.7 years) were analyzed. In the internal test set, the DLRN achieved an AUC of 0.852, higher than the clinical (0.673; p = 0.001), original radiomics (0.765; p = 0.030), and combined radiomics (0.793; p = 0.050) models. In the external test set, the DLRN remained robust (AUC = 0.829) and outperformed the clinical, original radiomics, and combined radiomics models (AUC = 0.680, 0.681, and 0.743; all p < 0.005). With DLRN assistance, radiologists showed improved diagnostic performance.

42993453.label: Conclusion
42993453.text: The MRI-based DLRN showed robust discrimination between FIGO 2023 stage I and stage II-IV EC across test sets, supporting its potential for preoperative risk stratification and decision support.

42993453.label: Key points
42993453.text: Question The introduction of the FIGO 2023 staging system has made the differentiation between stages more challenging, highlighting the need for better tools. Findings A new MRI-based deep-learning radiomics nomogram (DLRN) accurately identifies high-risk patients, significantly outperforming traditional and individual clinical prediction methods. Critical relevance statement This tool helps doctors make better preoperative treatment plans, potentially improving patient outcomes in endometrial cancer.

43002603.text: Focal nodular hyperplasia (FNH) in young children may mimic malignancy when large and markedly hypervascular. A 5-year-old girl with no known predisposing factors presented with painless abdominal distension and hepatomegaly. Serum alpha-fetoprotein and beta-human chorionic gonadotropin were normal. MRI showed a hypervascular hepatic mass with stellate central scar, abnormal intralesional vessels, and intrahepatic arteriovenous shunting, concerning for fibrolamellar hepatocellular carcinoma (FLHCC). Subsequent ⁹⁹ᵐTc-sulfur-colloid scintigraphy demonstrated near-homogeneous tracer uptake within the lesion, mildly lower than the normal liver. The preserved Kupffer-cell function favored FNH, likely arising as a hyperplastic response to altered local perfusion. Clinical surveillance supported the benign diagnosis.

43018703.label: Objectives
43018703.text: To evaluate the impact of fat saturation on T2-weighted (T2W) imaging in the assessment of small renal masses (SRMs; cT1a ≤ 4 cm) with the clear cell likelihood score (ccLS).

43018703.label: Methods
43018703.text: This retrospective study included 147 histologically confirmed SRMs evaluated with MRI including non-fat saturated (NFS) and fat saturated (FS) T2W fast spin echo acquisitions. Two readers (R1, R2) assigned qualitative T2 signal categories (hypo-, iso-, hyperintense), with sequence-specific ccLS scores recalculated while all non-T2 ccLS components were held constant. Agreement, sequence-related reclassification, and inter-reader agreement were assessed for T2 signal intensity and ccLS scores. Cumulative link mixed models (CLMMs) were used to assess sequence-related shifts in ordinal category. Quantitative mass-to-cortex signal-intensity ratios were compared between sequences using Bland-Altman analysis.

43018703.label: Results
43018703.text: Qualitative agreement between sequences was 74% and 65% for R1 and R2, respectively. FS-T2W was associated with over four-fold greater cumulative odds of a higher qualitative T2 signal category than NFS-T2W (OR, 4.68; 95% CI, 2.91-7.52; p < 0.001), with upgrading in 20% (R1) and 30% (R2) of lesions versus downgrading in 5% for both readers. Qualitative inter-reader agreement was substantial (κ = 0.77 for NFS-T2W; κ = 0.73 for FS-T2W). Mass-to-cortex ratios were higher on FS-T2W (median 1.30 vs. 1.15; p < 0.001), corresponding to a mean proportional increase of 17.9% (95% CI, 12.4-23.4%). ccLS concordance remained high between NFS-T2W and FS-T2W (R1: 94% and R2: 90%; weighted κ = 0.944 and 0.918). FS-T2W was associated with greater cumulative odds of a higher ccLS category than NFS-T2W (OR, 4.27; 95% CI, 1.52-12.0; p = 0.006). Inter-reader agreement for ccLS was almost perfect (weighted κ = 0.98 for NFS-T2W; 0.95 for FS-T2W).

43018703.label: Conclusion
43018703.text: Fat saturation introduces a systematic upward bias in qualitative T2 signal assessment of small renal masses. Although ccLS reclassification was less frequent and overall agreement remained high, this bias may alter ccLS assignment, particularly in lesions with inherently low T2 signal intensity, supporting standardized NFS-T2W acquisition when applying the ccLS.

43083903.label: Purpose
43083903.text: Accurate preoperative localisation of hyperfunctioning parathyroid glands enables minimally invasive parathyroidectomy (MIP) in primary hyperparathyroidism (pHPT). This umbrella review summarises more than a decade of meta-analytic evidence on preoperative localisation imaging.

43083903.label: Methods
43083903.text: Twenty-eight systematic reviews (published 2012-2025) were identified through a PubMed search and assessed within a predefined inclusion period (2011-2026). The analysis covered ultrasonography (US), [99mTc]Tc-methoxyisobutylisonitrile ([99mTc]Tc-MIBI) scintigraphy with single-photon emission computed tomography/computed tomography (SPECT/CT), four-dimensional CT (4D-CT), and [11C]methionine and [18F]fluorocholine positron emission tomography/CT (PET/CT). Pooled sensitivity, specificity, positive predictive value (PPV), and detection rate (DR) were extracted, using histopathology and, where available, postoperative biochemical cure as reference standard.

43083903.label: Results
43083903.text: Pooled sensitivity/specificity was 80%/77% for US and 84%/87% for [99mTc]Tc-MIBI scintigraphy. Detection rates were 84-88% for SPECT/CT, 74% for SPECT alone, and 70% for planar scintigraphy. Multiphase CT achieved 73% per-quadrant and 81% per-side sensitivity; after negative or inconclusive scintigraphy, 4D-CT reached 71% sensitivity and 81% PPV. [11C]methionine PET/CT sensitivities ranged from 77 to 86%. Radiolabelled choline ([11C]choline and [18F]fluorocholine) PET performed best (pooled sensitivity 95%, PPV 97%, DR 91%). [18F]fluorocholine outperformed [99mTc]Tc-MIBI scintigraphy (96% vs. 54% per patient), [11C]methionine (92% vs. 80% per lesion, indirect comparison) and 4D-CT (92% vs. 85% per patient). In the largest choline meta-analysis (1,716 patients), pooled sensitivity was 93.8% and the surgical cure rate 92.8%.

43083903.label: Conclusion
43083903.text: Among currently available techniques, [18F]fluorocholine PET/CT provides the highest diagnostic accuracy for preoperative localisation of hyperfunctioning parathyroid glands. It consistently surpasses conventional scintigraphy and 4D-CT in sensitivity while entailing lower radiation exposure.
